about: Every rule a published number rests on: its version, the card that checks it, what it was tuned on, what it was checked on without tuning, when its pass bar was set, and every revision with the reason and the effect. Rules tried and dropped are listed too.

rules.rule: A job is flaky when the same code failed and passed: a re-run of the same run, or another run on the same tree.
rules.pass_bar: event precision lower bound at least 85%
rules.result: met (92-99%); ties the plain retry rule scored on the retries it can see (96.9%); history confirms 42 of 112 flagged flakes as not the change and can't refute any

revisions.why: all 3 flips that weren't real flakes, and 5 checks of the PR's own text, were pull-request runs of workflows that also run on PR edits or labels
revisions.effect: 9 of 108 events left out (3 wrong, 5 PR-text checks, 1 real timing flake); 99 of 99 kept are real

revisions.from: pull-request flips left out in PR-edit workflows
revisions.why: held out, all 17 flips in such workflows were real flakes

rules.rule: A pull request's job failure is called known flaky (shown as "Likely flaky: check the error, then re-run it", never "safe") only when the job had 3+ flakes in the window, one in the failing step; the failing step's log, up to its first error, shows an outside service, the runner or a wait failing and no failing test; and no line there names a file the pull request changed. A changed file named reads "maybe yours"; anything else reads "flaked before" (look first). It never passes the verdict check on its own.
rules.tuned_on: masking.py's 36 failures in 9 repos and the first held-out read's 108 calls in 15 repos (heldout.py), which counted as tuning once it was used to write this rule
rules.held_out: pre-registered 2026-10-28 (flaky/README.md), then scored on a fresh read of 36 repos none of the earlier reads used: 197 known-flaky calls by history in 19 jobs and 9 repos, 44 labelled at most 3 per job (flaky/safe-rule-results.json)
rules.result: bar not met: the rule kept 4 of the 44 fresh calls (9%; 3 jobs, 2 repos), none the change's own (0 of 4, 0-49%); 73 clear calls with none caused would be needed. On the data it was written from, 0 of 31 and 0 of 8. The history rule alone: 5 of 22 clear fresh calls caused (23%)

revisions.why: 15 of 34 failures it called safe were caused by the change (44%)
revisions.effect: 7 called safe (5 clearly labelled, 0 caused), all one job; the other 29 now cost a look

revisions.from: a known flake passed the verdict check
revisions.why: 13 of 81 held-out safe calls were the change's own failure; matching past flakes' errors didn't separate them
revisions.effect: known flaky still reads 'likely a flake, re-run it', but the verdict check passes only once CI is green

revisions.from: a known flake read 'likely a flake, re-run it'
revisions.why: in the agent head-to-head a smaller model trusted it on 2 failures the change caused
revisions.effect: it asks to check the error isn't from the change before re-running; those 2 were then answered right

revisions.from: 3+ flakes in the window, one in the failing step (history alone); shown as "Known flaky"
revisions.why: held out, 13 of 81 such calls were the change's own failure; a flake's sign in the failing step's log and no changed file named separated them on the tuning data (0 of 31 caused when both held; 8 of 8 clear caused when a changed file was named)
revisions.effect: fresh read: 4 of 44 calls kept, 0 caused (0-49%), so the 5% bar is unproven; shown as "Likely flaky" with its evidence, never "safe"; the rest read flaked before, or maybe yours (4 of 5 clear fresh cases caused)

rules.strength_why: too few calls to show 5%: the label says "likely", the advice says to check the error first, and the verdict check waits for a green re-run

rules.rule: The failing step's log shows a registry, cache, network or runner error and no failing tests.
rules.tuned_on: the 284 labelled failures it is scored on (signatures written from common errors, then checked there)
rules.held_out: 633 unlabelled failures from the same reads (flaky/outside-fresh-results.json), judged by re-runs and the default branch
rules.pass_bar: none caused by the change among matches
rules.result: tuning set: 35 matched, none caused (90-100%); held out: 41 matched, none of 38 clearly labelled caused (0-9%); fresh: 5 of 8 history-decided matches not caused, the other 3 one repo's lasting registry rate limit

revisions.from: failure-section match including 'failed to download and build'
revisions.why: a dependency's own build failing matched
revisions.effect: taken out; 4 matches given up for safety

revisions.why: ninja's 'FAILED:' build lines hid an sccache outage

dropped.rule: withhold 'outside failure' when the pull request edits CI files
dropped.why: on 36 fresh matches it caught none of the change-caused cases and took the excuse from 4 real outages

rules.rule: A pull request's job failure reads already failing on main when the default branch failed in the same step in the 3 days before with the same error (2 of every 3 error lines shared); it still blocks the verdict check.
rules.tuned_on: 23 labelled pull-request failures in 12 repos whose step had just failed on the default branch (flaky/already-results.json)
rules.held_out: 60 held-out candidates in a second, wider read
rules.pass_bar: caused by the change at most 5% at the upper bound before it may pass the verdict check
rules.result: not shown: same error 1 of 6 held out (only 11 of 60 matched), 0 of 12 tuned; the step alone 5 of 51 held out

revisions.why: 4 of 22 such failures were caused by the change, with a different error in that step

rules.strength_why: 1 of 6 held-out matches with the same error

rules.rule: A failure with no flake history whose failing step (or test message) shows a wait or deadline running out, a benchmark gate or a live service in a test reads maybe flaky (re-run once to tell); it still blocks.
rules.tuned_on: the 284 labelled logs and the agent card's misses (flaky/maybe-results.json)
rules.pass_bar: caused by the change at most 20% at the upper bound (it asks for a re-run, it doesn't excuse)
rules.result: fits: 0 of 22 tuned; held out the signs matched only 2 of 150 (1 the change's): too rare to judge

revisions.from: track record over all 24 signature matches
revisions.why: the product says maybe flaky only for never-flaked failures (a whole-release review)
revisions.effect: the track record counts never-flaked matches: 1 of 6 (0 of 4 tuning, 1 of 2 held out)

rules.rule: A failure that would read likely flaky, flaked before or maybe flaky, whose flakes in the last 30 days all came from this same pull request (none on the default branch or other pull requests), reads new: a race or order dependence the change added fails now and then and passes on a re-run.
rules.tuned_on: none: a public suggestion (2026-10-31) with the failure it describes written as tests
rules.held_out: not yet replayed on the labelled pull-request failures
rules.pass_bar: none set yet; it only moves a call toward the change and never excuses a failure
rules.result: untested on labels: the replay needs the held-out reads again
rules.strength_why: not yet measured on labelled failures

rules.rule: A likely flake that failed 2 or more times on this pull request's runs, where that many failures would come from its default-branch rate (smoothed by one failure and one pass, over 10 or more runs) less than 5% of the time, reads new: the change made a flaky check fail more often.
rules.tuned_on: none: a public suggestion (2026-10-31) with the failure it describes written as tests
rules.held_out: not yet measured; the plan is regressions seeded into repos of the stackvitals organisation
rules.pass_bar: none set yet; it only moves a call toward the change and never excuses a failure
rules.strength_why: not yet measured on seeded or labelled failures

rules.rule: A pull-request failure in a workflow that also runs when the PR's title, description or labels change, with no failing test in the step, whose error lines are about the PR (the pull request, a PR title or label, a label to add or missing, a checkbox, checklist or template left unchecked or incomplete), reads PR details: fix the PR, not the code; it still blocks.
rules.tuned_on: the agent head-to-head's misses (agents/results2.json): 9 such failures in 4 repos, called known flaky or new
rules.held_out: none apart from the tuning repos: all 231 labelled pull-request failures (47 repos) were scored, the 9 included
rules.pass_bar: caused by the change's code at most 20% at the upper bound (it changes the advice, it doesn't excuse)
rules.result: 1 of 24 matches the change's code (1-20.2%), in 4 repos: at the bar's edge, from a small sample; 21 of the 24 had read known flaky

revisions.from: error lines mentioning a title, label or description anywhere
revisions.why: a test assertion about chart labels matched
revisions.effect: the words must be about the PR

revisions.from: only jobs whose steps read the PR (triggers.metadata_jobs)
revisions.why: label checks gated by `if:` and checks reading the PR in a script were missed (2 matches of 24)
revisions.effect: any job of a workflow run by PR edits, with the error guard

revisions.why: a whole-release review: a template rendering error in a CI workflow run on labels matched
revisions.effect: those words need the PR's wording beside them, and a failing test rules it out; still 24 of 24 matched

rules.strength_why: 24 matches in 4 repos, one repo gave most

rules.rule: Deployments API to production, else deploy workflows unless a side service, else non-prerelease releases, else release workflows; workflow names matched on deploy, release, publish or push-image minus 47 deny words.
rules.tuned_on: the delivery repos of the platform work
rules.held_out: 25 untuned repos (dora/sources-labels.csv), then 35 more drawn after the rule was fixed (dora/sources-more-labels.csv)
rules.result: 23 of 25, then 30 of 35 held out: 53 of 60 (78-94%); DevLake default 9 of 60, configured 22 of 60; workflow recall 60% on the held-out repos

revisions.from: display name checked against the deny list
revisions.why: a file named deploy.yml titled 'Check and Publish' hit the deny word 'check'
revisions.effect: a file named only deploy, release or publish ships whatever its display name; 22 to 23 of 25

rules.rule: A revert links to the pull request it undoes and the deployment that shipped it; never shipped when no deployment ran it.
rules.tuned_on: 18 reverts in 23 repos (the same set it is scored on)
rules.held_out: 99 reverts in 16 more repos chosen for the most reverts (dora/linkage-more-results.json)
rules.result: right on 87 of 89 links checked with the compare API across both samples (73 of 73 held out); time order wrong on 71 of 89

revisions.from: every revert counted as a failed deployment
revisions.why: 11 of 18 undid a change that never shipped
revisions.effect: never-shipped reverts are no failed deployment

rules.rule: People who answered 10+ others' issues or first-reviewed 2+ others' pull requests in a year, or who labelled, assigned, closed or marked as duplicate someone else's issue (only triage rights allow it), count as the project's responders.
rules.held_out: 400 comments from 86 other repos (labels-validation.csv); for version 2 the same set, used once for the decision
rules.result: held out: catches 57% of project answers weighted (47% before), 4 more answers; holds on either labeller's labels

revisions.why: triage acts mark people acting for the project; on the labelled comments the rule missed, they found 8 project answers among 11
revisions.effect: held out: 4 more project answers (47% to 57% weighted); on Claude's labels 45% to 53%, on Gemini's 32% to 38%

dropped.rule: also counting people with 3+ merged pull requests
dropped.why: caught 7 more points of project answers on the first set, but 9 of the 15 comments it added were drive-bys or other users' replies

rules.rule: Time to first project response with items still waiting kept in (Kaplan-Meier); an item closed unanswered is censored at closing.
rules.result: median counting waiting issues is 5.2 times the answered-only one

revisions.from: closed-unanswered items treated as still waiting
revisions.why: they stopped being at risk when they closed

rules.rule: Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.1 over every check in a scan, on p-values calibrated against the repo's past 8 weeks (typical swing 1.5 for times, each past week capped at a four-sigma swing); pickup and opened-to-merged time are also checked over 14 days, calibrated on past windows that don't overlap them.
rules.tuned_on: swing chosen on half of 20 public repos; the cap on halves of 29
rules.held_out: the other halves; the replay on 26 repos
rules.pass_bar: at most 10% of shuffled scans flag anything
rules.result: 7.5% (met); 10x slowdowns caught 25% in their first week, 35% in their second

revisions.why: in a slowdown's second week the weekly check's baseline holds the first slow week, so 10x slowdowns were caught in 15% of scans
revisions.effect: on the same replay, second-week catches of 10x slowdowns 15% to 35%, first-week 31% to 25%, false alarms 7.4% to 7.5%; CUSUM charts tried and dropped (no gain)

rules.rule: A small repo's first-try share pulled toward its peer group's beta-binomial prior (maximum likelihood, groups of 20+).
rules.tuned_on: half of 6,623 repos fit the priors
rules.pass_bar: lower out-of-sample error under 30 pushes; ranges cover 90-97%
rules.result: 29% less squared error at 3 pushes; 94.6% coverage (met)

rules.rule: Agents' and AI-marked PRs compared within the same repo, month and size band (Mantel-Haenszel with Sato's variance).
rules.pass_bar: shuffled AI labels' range includes zero

rules.rule: An incident is linked to the last production deployment (or release) finished before it was reported (DevLake's rule).
rules.held_out: 60 regression and incident issues naming a version, 39 crawl repos; 15 named the release that broke
rules.pass_bar: none set before sampling: a first measurement of a rule we adopted from DevLake
rules.result: right 6 of 15 (40%, 20-64%); the version the report names: 10 of 15, held out 4 of 9 against 2 of 9 (p 0.5): kept, with the caveat in docs/dora-guide.md
rules.strength_why: 15 reports named the release that broke

rules.rule: Throughput, people's merged PRs, review wait and merge rate after a repo starts taking agents' PRs, by staggered difference-in-differences against repos that haven't started (preregistration.md).
rules.pass_bar: leads and the 3-month-earlier negative control include zero
rules.result: merge rate: no measurable change (-2.7 to +0.7 points); throughput and review wait: not credible (adopters already growing)

rules.rule: A PR is an agent's (agent account or agent branch) or AI-assisted (AI trailer in its last 5 commits or its description, an agent task link in the description, or an AI label in any spelling).
rules.tuned_on: odd ids of 400 labelled PRs (v2 additions: Jules links, label spellings)
rules.pass_bar: precision of 95% or more; recall reported as a floor
rules.result: met: 191 of 194 (95.5-99.5%); recall 78.8% weighted, 66.3% on the held-out half

revisions.from: AI trailers in the last 5 commits, labels matched exactly, agent account or branch
revisions.why: 5 of 23 missed PRs named the tool in their description; label spellings and Jules task links missed in the tune half
revisions.effect: recall 75.0% to 78.8% weighted (63.9% to 66.3% held out); precision 185 of 187 to 191 of 194

labellers: Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite (second, same codebook and evidence)
labels.adjudication: Claude, blind to which labeller gave which label
labels.history_check: flaky/natural-results.json: GitHub's recorded re-runs and flakes on other changes, and earlier default-branch runs for 'caused' (never the failure's own run), decide 48 of 263 flaky failures with no labeller; on their definite answers Claude's labels agree on all 47, Gemini's 81%, against 92% for always answering 'not caused'
